Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1a) demonstrates a homogeneous opacity in the right upper lobe that appears to respect the horizontal fissure inferiorly. This appearance, often described as a "reverse S sign" or simply a lobar consolidation pattern that doesn't cross fissures, is characteristic of an obstructing mass like adenocarcinoma causing post-obstructive pneumonia or collapse, rather than a simple infectious pneumonia which typically crosses fissures or has fluffy borders.
